notes: Scotts Miracle-Gro Co (NYSE: SMG). Largest US consumer lawn & garden brand (Scotts, Miracle-Gro, Roundup distribution agreement) plus Hawthorne Gardening (indoor / hydroponics, Gen 1 cannabis-cultivation supplier). Fiscal year ends last Saturday of September. Data from SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000825542). EBITDA = operating income + D&A. Net debt = LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent − cash. FY21 was peak (COVID gardening boom + Hawthorne hydroponics demand pull from cannabis legalization wave); FY22-24 collapse driven by post-COVID consumer rollback PLUS Hawthorne cannabis-segment crash (revenue fell from $1.4B FY21 to <$300M by FY24, multi-billion goodwill writedowns). Heavy debt-paydown campaign FY23-25; FY25 profitability returning to core US Consumer.

periods.notes: FY21: peak year. Revenue $4.93B (+19% YoY) on COVID lawn/garden boom + Hawthorne hydroponics (cannabis cultivation pull-through). Op income $723M + D&A $93.8M = EBITDA $816.8M. Net income $512.5M, EPS $9.20.

FY22: revenue −20% YoY to $3.92B as COVID gardening reversed. Op loss −$434M (Hawthorne goodwill / asset writedowns) + D&A $105.2M = EBITDA −$328.8M. Net loss −$437.5M, EPS −$7.88. Net debt swelled to $2.88B.
FY23: revenue $3.55B (−9.5%); Hawthorne segment continued bleeding (revenue cut in half). Op loss −$174M + D&A $92.5M = EBITDA −$81.9M. Net loss −$380.1M, EPS −$6.79.

FY24: revenue flat at $3.55B but margin recovery — op income $208.8M + D&A $80.6M = EBITDA $289.4M (vs −$82M FY23). Net loss −$34.9M (interest expense + remaining Hawthorne charges). Debt paydown $383M YoY.

FY25: revenue $3.41B (−4%) but full margin restoration — op income $358.6M + D&A $62.7M = EBITDA $421.3M. Net income $145.2M, EPS $2.52 — first profitable year since FY21. Net debt $2.07B (-$813M from FY22 peak). Hawthorne now <8% of mix; consumer core stabilized.
